whatItIs.text: Rice parboiled, dried, and pounded into flat flakes — poha in India, chiura in Nepal, khao mao in Thailand — which cook (or just soak) in minutes.

historyNote.text: Flattened rice runs deep in wedding culture: in Nepal's Newar ceremony, pounded rice is part of the bride price, and the groom must ask for it three times, each using a less formal word for 'you'.

howToChoose.text: Thin flakes for soaking into poha-style dishes, thick for frying; the bag should smell fresh and starchy, with no dampness or mould risk from clumping.

storage.text: Keep dry and airtight in a cool cupboard. The rulebook has the details.

foodSafetyRef.note: dry-goods storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Rinse, soak briefly, and squeeze dry for Indian poha with onion and turmeric; a handful of flakes crisps in hot oil into a snack or a biryani topping.

substitutions.note: different texture; works for quick savoury breakfasts
